Verdict: REVISE — narrowly, for the omitted charge definition and ledger identityThe all-width construction, acyclic freezing proof, odd-width tile geometry, forced receiver labels, and automatic cross-component packing argument are correct. I find no geometric or freezing counterexample to the package.The remaining gap is in the compensation statement as a self-contained claim: the supplied note does not define the original  $\rho$ , the auxiliary fields  $s,r,d$ , or “deficient,” and it does not state the identity linking total charge to  $|T|+|M|-mn/2$ . The numerical tuples and a filename reference do not establish those identifications.I can independently prove the exact, unambiguous count identity
$$\boxed{
|T\cap V_R|+|M_H|-\frac{|V_R|}{2}=-1.
}$$
If the original ledger satisfies
$$\rho(Q)=t_Q+\frac{p_Q}{2}-2$$
—or the equivalent expression using internal matching edges and crossing endpoints—then every numerical charge and compensation conclusion in the note follows. Including or precisely importing the actual ledger definition would resolve this revision.This is a review of the written mathematics. I have not executed code or Lean, verified the reported test totals, or reviewed the coordinate and packing adapters.1. The family and actual matching are correct for every  $w\ge3$ Put  $q=w\bmod2$ . The matching admits the uniform description
$$e_j=\bigl\{(j\bmod2,j-1),(j\bmod2,j)\bigr\},
\qquad 0\le j\le w.
\tag{1}$$
This includes the specially listed initial edge.These edges are pairwise vertex-disjoint:consecutive indices use opposite rows;indices of the same parity use disjoint consecutive column pairs.Their endpoints are exactly
$$H=(\{0,1\}\times\{0,\ldots,w-1\})
\cup\{(0,-1),(q,w)\}.$$
Thus  $M$  is an actual perfect matching of  $H$ , with  $w+1$  edges.The six supports are distinct and pairwise nonadjacent for all  $w\ge3$ . In particular, the minimum same-exterior-row separation is three columns, so the small widths do not introduce an exceptional support adjacency.Each selected support has exactly its intended endpoint neighbor. The endpoint occupied-degree classification is also correct:each tail has one endpoint neighbor and two selected supports;each opposite-row end corner has two endpoint neighbors and one support;every other endpoint has three endpoint neighbors.Therefore the baseline is feasible and every endpoint has occupied degree exactly three.The counts
$$|T|=6,\qquad |P|=2w+2,\qquad |M|=w+1,\qquad |T|+|M|=w+7$$
are correct. The only all- $P$  unit squares lie in the central rectangle, so there are exactly  $w-1$ .These exact global counts and degree equalities describe the baseline. Arbitrary feasible completions can add occupied vertices elsewhere and can add exterior neighbors to some endpoints; they do not invalidate the freezing certificate or the receiver-label arguments below.2. The two-step freezing wave is valid and acyclicThe wave also has a uniform formula:
$$z_j=(j\bmod2,j-1),
\qquad
m(z_j)=(j\bmod2,j),
\qquad 0\le j\le w.
\tag{2}$$
Every  $z_j$  has odd checkerboard color. The  $w+1$  vertices  $z_j$  are one endpoint from each matching edge, so they are exactly the odd-color endpoints of  $H$ .The initial two steps are correctly grounded: $z_0=(0,-1)$  freezes from its two original  $T$ -supports.Its mate  $(0,0)$  is consequently necessarily occupied. $z_1=(1,0)$  then freezes from that retained neighbor and the support  $(2,0)$ .For  $0\le j\le w-2$ ,
$$z_{j+2}=(j\bmod2,j+1).$$
Its two certified neighbors are
$$m(z_j)=(j\bmod2,j)$$
and
$$m(z_{j+1})=((j+1)\bmod2,j+1).$$
The first incidence is horizontal; the second is vertical. The two vertices are distinct.Thus every inductive step uses mates of two vertices already frozen. No step requires a retained mate to remain labeled  $P$ ; remaining occupied is sufficient. There is no circular retention premise.The reflection supplies exactly the complementary waveFor the stated parity-dependent map  $J$ , direct substitution gives
$$J(e_j)=e_{w-j},
\qquad
J(z_j)=m(z_{w-j}).
\tag{3}$$
The map also exchanges the three pairs of prescribed supports and flips checkerboard color in both parity cases.Consequently the reflected wave is the reverse mate sequence of the first wave. It is disjoint from the first wave and contains all remaining endpoints. Every endpoint of  $H$  is therefore universally frozen.One useful scope clarification is that  $J$  need preserve only the prescribed finite matching-and-support pattern. It need not preserve an arbitrary completed exterior or every unused padding column. All incidences used in the reflected certificate remain present, which is sufficient.Under arbitrary exterior completion, the precise conclusion is:No feasible global bundle can use a matching edge of  $H$ .Additional components may admit promotions of their own. In the displayed baseline there are no such components, so no nonempty promotion sequence can begin.3. The tile geometry is correct, including the odd three- $P$  end tileLet
$$n=\left\lfloor\frac w2\right\rfloor,
\qquad w=2n+q.$$
Because the translation is even in both coordinates, it suffices to work with the normalized even tiling.The receiver tiles are exactly:
$$L=\{0,1\}\times\{-2,-1\},$$

$$C_i=\{0,1\}\times\{2i,2i+1\},
\qquad 0\le i<n,$$
and
$$E=\{0,1\}\times\{2n,2n+1\}.
\tag{4}$$
Here are the physical counts that can be verified without any undefined ledger terminology:Tile $T$  $P$ BlanksInternal matching edgesEndpoints matched outside the tileEach central  $C_i$  $0$  $4$  $0$  $1$  $2$ Left  $L$  $1$  $1$  $2$  $0$  $1$ Right  $E$ , even  $w$  $1$  $1$  $2$  $0$  $1$ Right  $E$ , odd  $w$  $0$  $3$  $1$  $1$  $1$ Central tilesThe lower internal edge of  $C_i$  is the matching edge with index  $2i+1$ . Its two upper endpoints are matched across the left and right tile boundaries.This remains true for the first and last central tiles. The end crossings are real matching incidences and are correctly retained in the accounting.Odd right endFor  $w=2n+1$ , the right tile is
$$E=\{0,1\}\times\{w-1,w\}.$$
Its three endpoints are exactly
$$(0,w-1),\qquad (1,w-1),\qquad (1,w).$$
The missing corner is  $(0,w)$ .The lower edge
$$(1,w-1)--(1,w)$$
is internal. The upper endpoint  $(0,w-1)$  is matched to  $(0,w-2)$  across the left boundary.Thus the odd tile has one internal matching edge and one crossing endpoint. There is no omitted endpoint or matching incidence. Under the physical excess formula, its charge is
$$0+1+\frac12-2=-\frac12,$$
exactly as claimed.The odd-width freezing reflection need not preserve the even tiling. That causes no defect: the note counts the odd right tile separately instead of treating it as a reflected one- $P$  end tile.4. Full receiver labels really are forced under arbitrary feasible completionsThis argument is sound and is stronger than merely observing that the baseline has certain blanks.Left endThe selected vertex  $(0,-2)$  already has the occupied tail neighbor  $(0,-1)$ . Therefore its neighbor  $(1,-2)$  cannot be occupied at all.The remaining site  $(1,-1)$  has two endpoint neighbors:
$$(0,-1),\qquad (1,0).$$
It cannot be  $T$ , because that would give it two occupied neighbors. It cannot be  $P$ , because it would join the whole endpoint component  $H$ , whose endpoint set is required to remain the stated one. It must be blank.This fixes all four labels of  $L$ .Even right endThe reflected argument fixes the two blanks in the even right end tile. In particular, one blank is forced by the axial selected support, and the other by its two neighbors in  $H$ .Odd right endThe only unlisted corner is  $(0,w)$ , with endpoint neighbors
$$(0,w-1),\qquad (1,w).$$
It is excluded from  $T$  by feasibility and excluded from  $P$  by completeness of  $H$ . Hence it is blank.ConsequenceEvery central tile is already fully  $P$ , and the preceding arguments fix every site in both end tiles. Retaining the actual matching also fixes all internal matching edges and crossing endpoint incidences.Therefore arbitrary feasible exterior completions cannot change the receiver’s physical labels or these matching counts.This proves invariance of any charge defined from those fixed data. Identifying that invariant quantity with the named original  $\rho$  requires the ledger definition—that is the outstanding issue, not a failure of the forced-label proof.5. The one-unit receiver deficit is independently verifiableThe aggregate counts in the note are correct:
$$|R|=n+2,\qquad
T_R=2-q,\qquad
P_R=2w+2,\qquad
B_R=4-q.
\tag{5}$$
Their sum is
$$T_R+P_R+B_R=4(n+2),$$
as required.All  $w+1$  matching edges have both endpoints in  $V_R$ , the union of the receiver tiles. More explicitly:the number of internal matching edges, summed over receiver tiles, is  $n+q$ ;the number of matching edges crossing between receiver tiles is  $n+1$ .Their sum is  $2n+q+1=w+1$ . Thus no internal or crossing contribution has been discarded.The following calculation is independent of the missing ledger notation:
$$\begin{aligned}
|T\cap V_R|+|M_H|-\frac{|V_R|}{2}
&=(2-q)+(w+1)-2(n+2)\\
&=(2-q)+(2n+q+1)-2n-4\\
&=-1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}$$
So the receiver has exactly one unit of deficit relative to half its number of sites, for both parities.What is needed to call this the original  $\rho$ If the original ledger satisfies
$$\rho(Q)
=t_Q+\frac{p_Q}{2}-2,
\tag{7}$$
then all three displayed tile charges follow immediately.Equivalently, if  $h_Q$  counts internal matching edges and  $d_Q$  counts endpoints matched outside the tile, then
$$p_Q=2h_Q+d_Q$$
and
$$\rho(Q)
=t_Q+h_Q+\frac{d_Q}{2}-2.
\tag{8}$$
Under (7) or (8), the central tiles have charge zero and the two end tiles each have charge  $-1/2$ . Thus this is one unit of actual negative tile charge, not merely a net deficit concealing a larger collection of negative and positive contributions.But the supplied excerpt does not state that (7) or (8) is the original ledger. Nor does it define the  $s,r,d$  fields and “deficient.” Those definitions must be included or imported precisely before the full tuples and original-ledger identification can be certified.The per-square limitation followsOnce the charge identification is supplied, the claimed limitation is correct. The receiver contains  $w-1$  unit squares and  $n$  aligned full- $P$  tiles, while its total available negative charge remains one.For any fixed  $\alpha>0$ , assigning  $\alpha$  units from this receiver to every unit square would require
$$\alpha(w-1)\le1,$$
which fails for sufficiently large  $w$ . The same argument applies to aligned full- $P$  tiles.The note properly limits this conclusion to the fixed endpoint-tile receiver. It supplies no bound on resources in an enlarged exterior region.6. Automatic cross-component packing is correctThe packing proof needs no additional collar-disjointness hypothesis.Let  $Q\in R_i$ . It contains an endpoint of  $H_i$ . The forced-label result proves that its complete  $P$ -set is a nonempty subset of  $H_i$ .If also  $Q\in R_j$ , it contains an endpoint of  $H_j$ . That endpoint would then belong to  $H_i$  as well, contradicting distinctness of the endpoint components.Hence
$$R_i\cap R_j=\varnothing
\qquad(i\ne j)
\tag{9}$$
as sets of physical tiles.This remains valid under the stated tile-preserving translations, reflections, and transposition. That qualification should apply to every allowed placement transformation. The odd-width reflection used in the freezing proof is a separate matter and is not needed for the packing argument.The proof establishes disjoint receivers from full tile-label rigidity, not merely from disjoint endpoint sets. That distinction is exactly what makes the argument work.7. The compensation implication follows once the ledger is specifiedSuppose charge is additive over physical tiles, and the receivers, sources, and remainder form the stated disjoint partition. Then
$$\rho(G)
=
\sum_{i=1}^{L}\rho(R_i)
+\sum_{j=1}^{K}\rho(S_j)
+\rho(\mathcal W).$$
Using the receiver values and source assumptions gives
$$\rho(G)
\le -L+K+\rho(\mathcal W).
\tag{10}$$
This part is a correct additive argument. It neither assumes nor proves that all positive sources can be covered.For an even-by-even ambient grid, formula (7) yields
$$\begin{aligned}
\rho(G)
&=\sum_Q\left(t_Q+\frac{p_Q}{2}-2\right)\\
&=|T|+\frac{|P|}{2}-\frac{mn}{2}\\
&=|T|+|M|-\frac{mn}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}$$
Therefore  $K\le L$  and  $\rho(\mathcal W)\le0$  imply
$$|T|+|M|\le\frac{mn}{2}.$$
If the original ledger uses a different formula, the note must instead state its actual additivity and the identity or inequality that links total charge to the objective. That link is indispensable to the last inference.The sufficient class itself is correctly scoped: receiver packing is proved; source coverage, the inequality  $K\le L$ , and the nonpositive remainder are additional conditions.8. Minor embedding clarificationThe stated dimensions do contain the construction. After translation by  $(2,2)$ , occupied rows lie in  $1,\ldots,4$ , and occupied columns lie in  $0,\ldots,w+3$ .There is not a complete blank border on all four sides:the left axial support lies in column  $0$ ;for even  $w$ , the right axial support lies in the last column.This is only a wording issue with “blank padding.” The embedding and all proofs are valid, and additional even padding can provide a full blank collar if desired.The ambient comparison is correct:
$$3W-(w+7)=2w+5+3q>0.$$
Thus the displayed baseline is comfortably below the half-area target.Required repair and final scopeTo make the package acceptable as a complete compensation theorem, include:The definition of the original tile charge  $\rho$ , and the auxiliary fields used in the displayed tuples.Its additivity over physical tiles.The identity or inequality connecting total charge to  $|T|+|M|-mn/2$ .If the actual original ledger is (7), or equivalently (8), these can be supplied in a short paragraph; the rest of the numerical argument is already proved above. The undefined auxiliary tuple fields can also be omitted if they are not needed, while retaining the verified physical counts and the actual charge definition.With that ledger identification supplied, I would return ACCEPT. There is no remaining odd-width, two-step-freezing, forced-label, or automatic-packing gap in the written arguments.The mathematical obstruction is correctly identified: arbitrary two-row endpoint shapes can be fully frozen with unboundedly many squares, while this fixed receiver has a constant one-unit deficit. That defeats the proposed shape normalization and fixed per-square payment from this receiver. The component-level compensation statement remains a conditional sufficient class and does not establish universal source coverage or refute the global grid inequality.
